references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 0
references.quote: The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this title, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 1
references.quote: (a) “Animal” means a live, vertebrate creature, domestic or wild, other than humans.

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 2
references.quote: (b) “Amphibian” is an animal that moves in and out of water (i.e., frogs and toads, newts and salamanders).

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 3
references.quote: (c) “Animal shelter” means any premises designated by City administrative authority for the purpose of impounding and caring for animals held under authority of this title, excluding wildlife, fowl and livestock.

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 4
references.quote: (d) “At large” means when an animal is not on the property of its owner and not under the physical control of the owner by leash or other similar device (voice or remote control only will not be considered adequate control).

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 5
references.quote: (e) “Attack” means any violent or aggressive physical action or contact.

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 6
references.quote: (f) “Bird” is an animal that bears its young in a hard-shelled egg, is covered with feathers and has forelimbs modified into wings, scaly legs and a beak, as opposed to teeth. See also “Fowl.”

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 7
references.quote: (g) “Cat” is an animal with soft fur, a short snout and retractile claws. A feral cat is a domesticated cat that has returned to the wild, or the offspring of such a cat. A feral cat is unsocialized to humans and has a temperament of extreme fear or resistance to contact with humans. An ear-tipped feral cat is a feral cat that exhibits a straight-line cutting of the tip of its left ear to indicate that it has been sterilized and vaccinated against rabies.

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 8
references.quote: (h) “Dangerous dog” shall mean any of the following:

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 9
references.quote: (1) Any dog with a known propensity or disposition to attack, to cause injury, or otherwise threaten the safety of human beings or domestic animals; or

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 10
references.quote: (2) Any dog which, in a vicious or threatening manner, approaches any person in apparent attack upon the person while on the streets, sidewalks, or any public grounds or places; or on private property other than on the property of the owner; or

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 11
references.quote: (3) Any dog which, unprovoked, attacks or bites, or has attacked or bitten, a human being or domestic animal; or

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 12
references.quote: (4) Any dog which was previously determined to be dangerous pursuant to the previous TMC 6.05.080 or the current TMC 6.15.170 ; or

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 13
references.quote: (5) Any dog owned or harbored primarily for the purpose of dog fighting shall only be considered dangerous if the dog is evaluated and dangerousness is concluded by a licensed veterinarian or a dog trainer certified by the Certification Council for Professional Dog Trainers with experience in evaluating dogs seized in similar cruelty cases.

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 14
references.quote: (6) Notwithstanding the definition of a “dangerous dog” above, no dog may be declared dangerous if any injury was sustained by a person under any of the following conditions:

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 15
references.quote: (i) The person was committing a willful trespass or other tort upon the premises occupied by the owner or keeper of the dog;

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 16
references.quote: (ii) The person was committing or attempting to commit a crime;

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 17
references.quote: (iii) The person provoked, teased, or injured the dog; or

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 18
references.quote: (iv) The dog was protecting itself, its owner, its offspring or another human being.

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 19
references.quote: (7) No dog may be declared dangerous if any injury was sustained by a domestic animal under any of the following conditions:

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 20
references.quote: (i) The domestic animal provoked, teased or injured the dog;

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 21
references.quote: (ii) The dog was protecting itself, its owner, its offspring or another human being; or

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 22
references.quote: (iii) The dog injures or kills an animal trespassing on the property of the dog’s owner.

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 23
references.quote: (8) Nothing in this chapter shall be deemed to regulate or prohibit the lawful maintenance and use of dogs by law enforcement agencies or include actions by a law enforcement dog while on duty or while performing duties.

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 24
references.quote: (i) “Dog” is an animal with a long or short snout, an acute sense of smell and a barking, howling or whining voice. A wild dog is an undomesticated dog that is found in the wild (i.e., the African wild dog, the dingo, the hyena and the wolf).

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 25
references.quote: (j) “Domestic animal” means one that is sufficiently tame to live with or near an individual owner or family, including, but not limited to, pets such as dogs, cats or miniature pot-belly pigs; or one that can be used to contribute to a family’s support, including, but not limited to, cattle, donkeys, goats, mules, poultry, sheep or swine. When something is domesticated, it is converted to domestic use, as in the case of a wild animal that is tamed. See also “Animal,” “Livestock” and “Pet.”

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 26
references.quote: (k) “Exotic animal” means a living mammal or marsupial that is normally found in the wild state, but shall not include a farm animal (livestock).

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 27
references.quote: (l) “Exposed to rabies” means an animal that has been bitten by, or subjected to danger, attack or harm by, any creature known to have been infected with rabies.

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 28
references.quote: (m) “Ferret” is a small animal, belonging to the weasel family, which usually weighs less than five pounds.

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 29
references.quote: (n) “Fish” is an animal that lives only in water and characteristically has fins, gills and a streamlined body (i.e., bony fishes, such as catfishes and tunas, and cartilaginous fishes, such as sharks and rays).

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 30
references.quote: (o) “Fowl” is a group of animals consisting of waterfowl or wildfowl. “Poultry” is a term typically used when referring to domesticated birds or fowl (i.e., chicken, duck, goose or turkey) that are raised for meat, eggs or feathers. See also “Bird.”

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 31
references.quote: (p) “Humane killing” means the painless administration of a lethal dose of an agent or method of euthanasia as prescribed in the Report of the American Veterinary Medical Association Panel on Euthanasia published in the Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association, March 1, 2001 (or any successor version of that report), that causes the painless death of an animal. Animals must be handled prior to administration of the agent or method of euthanasia in a manner to avoid undue apprehension by the animal.

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 32
references.quote: (q) “Humane society” means any animal shelter contracted with the City of Topeka that is licensed by the State of Kansas. See also “Animal shelter.”

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 33
references.quote: (r) “Invertebrate” is an animal that does not have a backbone or spinal column.

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 34
references.quote: (s) “Livestock” is a group of domesticated animals (i.e., cattle, donkeys, goats, horses, mules, poultry, sheep, swine and similar animals) that are raised in an agricultural setting to produce commodities such as food, fiber and labor. Livestock are often referred to as “useful animals,” which implies a commercial purpose of being reared for financial gain. See also “Domestic animal” and “Pet.”

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 35
references.quote: (t) “Miniature pot-belly pig” is a breed of small pig originating in southeastern Asia and having a straight tail, potbelly, swayback and typically having a black, white, or black and white coat.

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 36
references.quote: (u) “Neutered male” is a male animal that by operation has been made infertile to prevent conception or one that has been certified by a licensed veterinarian as being naturally infertile.

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 37
references.quote: (v) “Owner” means any person of legal age who keeps, possesses or harbors any animal. A parent or legal guardian shall be deemed to be an owner of animals owned or maintained by children upon their premises.

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 38
references.quote: (w) “Pet” means a tamed animal cared for by its owner and kept primarily for a person’s companionship and not as a food source. See also “Domestic animal” and “Livestock.”

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 39
references.quote: (x) “Rabbit” is a rodent-like animal with soft fur, long ears, a divided upper lip and long hind legs, known for burrowing.

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 40
references.quote: (y) “Reptile” is an animal with dry, scaly skin (i.e., lizards, snakes and turtles). Lizards have moderately elongated bodies, a tapering tail and two pairs of legs held outward from the body. Snakes are limbless and have elongated bodies; includes venomous and nonvenomous species. Turtles have trunks that are enclosed in a shell.

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 41
references.quote: (z) “Restrained” means confined by building, fence, leash, harness or other appropriate means, or is accompanied by a competent person and under the person’s immediate control by leash or held in arms.

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 42
references.quote: (aa) “Rodent” is a gnawing animal distinguished by strong, constantly growing incisors and no canine teeth (i.e., hamsters, mice, porcupines, rats and squirrels).

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 43
references.quote: (bb) “Secure enclosure” means a six-sided structure, counting the top and bottom, secured to the sides or embedded in the ground two feet or more for purposes of preventing a dangerous dog, as defined in subsection (h) of this section, from digging out. The structure must be equipped with a gate or door that is secured with a padlock or combination lock for purposes of preventing escape and ensuring that such gate or door cannot be opened by anyone other than the owner, keeper, possessor or harborer of the animal.

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 44
references.quote: (cc) “Spayed female” is a female animal that by operation has been made infertile to prevent conception; or one that has been certified by a licensed veterinarian as being naturally infertile.

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 45
references.quote: (dd) “Supervision” means within visual and auditory range of the owner.

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 46
references.quote: (ee) “Tether,” when used as a verb, means fastening an animal to a stationary object, pulley run line or stake. When used as a noun means a chain, leash, rope, cable, string, leather or nylon strap, or any other material used to fasten an animal to a stationary object, pulley run line or stake.

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 47
references.quote: (ff) “Vertebrate” is an animal that has a backbone or spinal column such as amphibians, birds, cats, dogs, ferrets, fish, fowl, livestock, miniature pigs, rabbits, reptiles and rodents.

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 48
references.quote: (gg) “Veterinary hospital” means any establishment maintained and operated by a licensed veterinarian for the diagnosis and treatment of diseases and injuries of animals.

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 49
references.quote: (hh) “Vicious” means a cross, ferocious or dangerous disposition; or a habit, tendency or disposition to snap, attack or bite any person, domestic animal or pet. (Ord. 20106 § 1, 12-19-17.)

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 50
references.quote: Cross References: Definitions generally, TMC 1.10.020 .

references.label: TMC 6.05.010 block 51
references.quote: State Law References: Kennels, K.S.A. 47-1721 .
